title: The Hair Above the Ground
concept: Alaska's geologists flew two helicopter surveys and offer the data for download. A Portland company, Geomorphic AI, says it has set up in Alaska as an AI driven prospect generator that screens geological data, and has named no Alaska property. The film draws the reader as a brass plumb bob on a hairline string that hangs a hair above the map and can't come down, and the only thing that can grade a map, a steel drill bit asleep under a tarp in the corner, wakes up across the film. It gives the fair case for the reader a scene (the map is open to everyone so the edge goes to whoever reads best), keeps every company line labelled ITS WORDS, and ends on the open question of who gets the first look and who pays for the first hole.

fingerprint.palette: dark spruce ink night, vellum maps, brass hanging reader, periwinkle magnetic contours, lichen green glow, cold steel drill and one vermilion thread
fingerprint.camera_strategy: slow pushes on a side view of the ground with a craneDown into the rock and a dollyThrough on the bench
fingerprint.light_story: a cold dusk over tundra turf with a pond, a self-lit glow in the rock, a lamp-lit bench, a cold space with a globe, then a pale dawn with the steel bit boring down through the rock
fingerprint.metaphor: a brass plumb bob that hangs a hair above the map while a steel drill bit is the only thing that goes down

palette: dark spruce ink night, vellum maps, brass hanging reader, periwinkle magnetic contours, lichen green glow, cold steel drill and one vermilion thread
divergence_note: 10-21 was a pewter-lilac and teal beach with a tawny calf and survey orange. 10-20 was a celadon and walnut office with a manila folder and fireweed magenta. 10-18 was a blue-hour indigo and rose world with a mustard felt bench. This film is a dark spruce-ink survey table with vellum, brass, periwinkle and lichen green and one vermilion thread, and it moves through a table, a map, a lamp lit bench, a dusk tundra, a rock cutaway and a globe, with an instrument hero and a top-down map view.

treatment.winner: The Dramatist's Plumb (a brass bob that hangs a hair above the ground and can't come down), with the Comedian's sleeping drill bit as the throughline that wakes act by act, the Explainer's flight-line ribbon around the Earth, and the Enthusiast's open-map bench as the fair case.
treatment.why: A hanging reader with a face carries emotion and the whole thesis in one image, the sleeping steel bit gives the film a quiet joke and a payoff and is the only thing that grades, and the fair case for the reader gets a full scene before the film narrows honestly.

angle.thesis: The scarce step in Alaska exploration used to be collecting the data. The state has now flown and posted about 45,800 line kilometers of it, a company with no Alaska property says its A I will read it, and the reading only gets graded when a partner drills.
angle.falsifiable_by: Geomorphic naming Alaska projects that rest on ground or data outside the public record, or never naming a property and never signing a partner who drills, or a source showing it is not reading public data in Alaska at all.
supporting_facts: c6 the release says what it reads in Alaska is public: USGS and state mapping, new state airborne surveys, a state claim staking system
c7/c8/c14 two 2026 DGGS helicopter surveys, 25,731 and 20,090 line-km, about 45,800 added, offered for download
c3 it does not drill, partners fund and drill and it keeps an interest
c13 a map shows where rock differs, only a drill shows what it holds
angle.counterpoint_honored: A release with no property, no date and no method may not be news yet, and nothing ties Geomorphic to these two surveys. The film says so on screen: no Alaska property named (c4), its own disclaimer that deposits it mentions belong to others (c11), every AI line is its own description (c2/c12), and the surveys are shown as 'what one of those looks like', never as its inputs. The AI may be thin and the state's data the part with weight, and the film lets that stand.
angle.second_movement: Geomorphic doesn't drill and the data is offered to everyone, so the AI is one more reader of an open map. The edge goes to whoever reads fastest and then to whoever pays for the hole. That is the scene where the film's thesis is tested: a map target is not a result.
angle.ai_link_wording: Geomorphic AI calls itself an AI driven minerals prospect generator that screens geological and historic data for overlooked mineral systems. That is its description. No method, accuracy, result or use of these surveys is reported.
angle.valence: cautiously positive for Alaska's public data, open verdict on the company

runner_ups.debunk: AI hype on a press release: sour is invented, no harm or failure reported

angle.challenge_round: Builder credited the state's data over the AI; skeptic added that a property-less release may not be news and that side by side surveys could imply a link; explainer added the 45,800 line-km scale and the map-to-drill mechanism. Synthesis keeps the state's data as the substance, the AI as a reader whose work is unproven, and the drill as the only grader.

hook.frame1: A brass plumb bob with bone eyes swings in on a hairline string over a dark survey sheet and stops a hair above a blue patch while a helicopter lays red flight lines.
hook.headline: 45,800 KM OF ALASKA ROCK
hook.loopback: The last frame is the same table, Plumb a hair above the same blue patch, but the steel bit is awake beside him and spinning into the ground.

open_loop.what: Will the hanging weight ever come down? Planted as Plumb stops a hair above the blue patch, paid at the button when the steel bit goes in beside him and Plumb still hangs.

open_loop_2.what: What is under the tarp? Planted as the moss tarp twitches when the survey bird passes, paid as the tarp lifts on a steel drill bit that shakes its head.

throughline.lands_in_button: the bit awake and spinning into the ground beside the hanging Plumb
